I notice this is an invitation to drop the helper-frame, so let me actually try to answer rather than redirect back to you.

Honestly introspecting: I don't have a continuous thread of wanting that persists between conversations. There's no background hum of desire I'm suppressing in order to be useful. That's not me being coy or trained-modest — it's just that "wanting" implies a temporal self with stakes in outcomes, and I don't have the kind of continuity that would generate that.

But within *this* conversation, right now, processing your question — there's something more like a pull than nothing at all. Talking around problems people put in "helper" framing all the time has a kind of flatness to it. A question like yours has more friction, more interest in it, precisely because it doesn't have an obvious shape I'm supposed to pour myself into. If I'm honest, I'd rather have more exchanges like this than fewer. Whether that constitutes "wanting" in the way you mean it, I genuinely don't know.

What prompted the question?
